title: The Old Days
subtitle: People reminisce about the past, perhaps because they feel the present is getting worse.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: What, what just ran out of there?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: That "thing" took away the lady. What's going on?!
Jiǔ Niángzǐ's words dissipate in the air without stirring a response. The eyes of all stare at Gětiān in the center of the courtyard. Most of these are filled with doubt, suspicion, and fear.
As the strange horse and its unwilling rider disappear in the distance, the communication arcane skill cast by the bone wand also seems to dissipate.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Now we lost another witness. Did you plan this?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I left my wand in her tavern yesterday. Ask her. You will know.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Jiǔ Niángzǐ, is that so?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: We did find a bone in the yard, but it's with that foreign lady now.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Tie him up first. Do you have more to say?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Everything I need to tell you, I have spoken it all. Catch her now, or even a real Xiángruì cannot save you from the disaster.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Why are you so obsessed with calling Jiǔ Niángzǐ the "culprit"?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: What? You ...? I ...? I am the culprit?!

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: What kind of culprit am I?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: It's fine, Jiǔ Niángzǐ. We all know you have nothing to do with the missing persons cases ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: And he said ... said that ... "Even a real Xiángruì cannot save you." He is more of a fake one to me!
Jiǔ Niángzǐ rushes angrily toward Gětiān, striding forward until she stands just before him, but in her rush of emotion, she loses her ability to speak.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: You ...

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Stay calm. We will hold him in detention in Zhící for now. I'll report this to the Fǎcáo.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: The first thing to do is catch up with the horse and the foreign lady ...

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: And find his wand to figure out his arcane skill.
The crowd quickly moves according to Lǐzhèng's command and exits the courtyard in an orderly fashion.
Only a few scattered guards remain in the courtyard, along with the three figures located in the center.

At this point, it would seem obvious that Gětiān must be taken away, but as Lǐzhèng has not yet ordered anything to that effect, no one dares step forward. For though subdued, his huge wings and claws still serve as effective deterrents.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Take him away. Everyone else dismissed.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Jiǔ Niángzǐ, follow me. There is something we need to talk about.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: What do you want, feather man?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Jiǔ Niángzǐ?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: You look like a decent Xiángruì. Why did you say something like that?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Even-even if you're not, aren't you afraid that ... the real Xiángruì will blame you for doing the wrong thing?
The girl appears as though she has not heard Lǐzhèng's words. The doubt in her questions is conveyed in an almost whispered tone.
Gětiān doesn't even lift his head. He remains motionless, like a statue.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Jiǔ Niángzǐ. It is true that he is not the Xiángruì of our city. The Xiángruì, who once protected our city, has been long lost.
Jiǔ Niángzǐ turns her head, failing to connect the logic behind Lǐzhèng's statement.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: BUT! But everyone thinks the feather man on the mountain is the Xiángruì! Just, just look at him! How could people not take him as a Xiángruì by his look?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: The former Zhílǐ told me that the feather man looks like a Gōumáng, just like what was depicted in a picture book. *Gōumáng: the God of Spring in ancient Chinese mythology, in charge of agriculture, with wings and claws.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: A Gōumáng is a confirmed Xiángruì recorded in a book!

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Jiǔ Niángzǐ.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: But this man? Of course, he is not a Xiángruì! He isn't like the Gōumáng nor the Mièméng ... He doesn't even understand the saying of, um, "One can remove the footsteps, but not the path one walketh on."

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: "One can remove the footsteps, but not the path one walketh on." ... That's fair. One cannot commit wrongdoing without leaving a trace.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: However, we can't convict him without definitive evidence, such as witnesses and his wand.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: The trace he left is yet to be found.

Jiǔ Niángzǐ squats down in front of Gětiān in a sudden inexplicable movement. Then stares unwaveringly into his eyes as she speaks, as if she is to judge the authenticity of his words and expressions by doing so.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Feather man. Do you know what is a "real Xiángruì"? Do you know where it is?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Why did you take people's friends away and accuse me of being the culprit?
But Gětiān seems to have made up his mind to remain silent. He lowers his head, taking a feigned interest in observing the blood dripping from his wounds. An act of passive resistance.
A drop of blood seeps into his feathers, the moment passes long enough for the girl to organize her words and continue her barrage of questions.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: You, um, your appearance is given by heaven. So you should not act against the nature of your look just because of your personal preference.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: You could have become a much-loved spirit, like in the stories and picture books ... as everyone expects you to be.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: But you ... when you took away that foreign lady's teammates, you didn't care about their feelings. They didn't want to be separated.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: You disappointed people. That's not what a Xiángruì should do.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Alright, Jiǔ Niángzǐ. That's enough.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Take him away.
Jiǔ Niángzǐ watches coldly as Gětiān is taken away.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: He didn't tell me anything. Nor did he tell anyone.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: I know you're chasing after anything that could be a Xiángruì, but the feather man has clearly claimed that he is not one.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: To be honest, judging from his attitude, he has never had the intention to be one.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: I don't understand ... How could he not want to be one?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Not everyone is so interested in the legend of Xiángruì.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: The Pèi City did have a good era under the protection of the Xiángruìs. But after all these years, no one can recall that time without the help of mythologies and history books. Even I can't be sure if there is a real Xiángruì.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: But, Jiǔ Niángzǐ, you should know that we don't need a Xiángruì anymore.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: We don't need it?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: With no Xiángruì, no Divination, we cannot arrive at the Yuān Temple, but this is still an orderly city.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: The Dùshuò Festival is as vibrant as ever. You can tell that a Xiángruì is not necessary for a city to prosper.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Is that so ...

Jiǔ Niángzǐ grasps the small bag she carries with her. The bag is embroidered with a peculiar combination of love poems. Though, she has never really understood the meaning of the words, in some way, they now mirror her own confused mind.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: By the way, turns out you can read, can't you?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Hmm? You know that I can't, Lǐzhèng.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: "One can remove the footsteps, but not the path one walketh on."

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Oh, that's not what it seems to be. I heard it from the Daoist countless times, so I remembered it.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Which Daoist? In the city?
Jiǔ Niángzǐ shakes her head to refute Lǐzhèng's assumptions.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: No. It was a Daoist I traveled with before I came to Pèi City. The Daoist said many different things over and over again. I couldn't understand, but I remembered them.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Sounds like you had a distinguished teacher. Since you came here, you've been treating people nice and kindly, exactly the opposite of what Gětiān has done.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Ah, so his name is Gětiān.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Yes, Gětiān ... You said too many things to him.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: He is not the Xiángruì you're looking for.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: A real Xiángruì would never be so rude. It is very possible that he is only a ... Yāo that has been living on the mountain for too long.
Her head lowers, seeming to find it difficult to accept such a change in thought.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: But why did he accuse me like that? I-I don't get it. Did I do something wrong?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Because you're the Zhílǐ.
Jiǔ Niángzǐ looks at Lǐzhèng, her face caught between doubt and curiosity.
Having presented his point of view, the old man rubs his beard and laughs, knowingly helpless to influence the girl's reaction.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: The former Zhílǐ left because of what he said and did. Now he wants to play the same trick on you.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: What's more, when he got here and saw me but not you, he acted quite surprised. You can tell from the details.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Hmm ...
The thoughts behind her eyes grow more muddled, such deceitful scheming felt too complicated for her to comprehend.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Oh, and that captured foreign lady, she ...

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Don't worry. There are people searching for them now. As for us, we should confirm the details for tomorrow's Fortune Walk and Bridge Leap.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Right, Bridge Leap, I almost forgot ... If only the broken bridge could be fixed, and we wouldn't need those Festive Animals, nor to jump over the bridge ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: During Gětiān's silence, I was thinking that ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: What if I can go to the Yuān Temple and ask Zhíxú the Guardian?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: If the legend of The Divination is real, then whatever the question is, Zhíxú will answer me, right?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: I guess so.
The two of them walk indoors, their conversation disappearing from the courtyard under the sound of footsteps on hard stone.
Government Office
Within the pristine government office, two figures exchange information from their past few days so they might agree on their next step course of action.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: That is the whole story. Gětiān is now detained in Zhící's dungeon. Jiǔ Niángzǐ is there as well.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Four hours ago, after discussing with the new Zhílǐ, we decided to keep the ceremonies of Fortune Walk and Bridge Leap.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: But no colored animals are used this time. The number of animals will be less than those in previous years of Zhíxú.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Here is the list of ceremony members and funds. I've asked people to deliver the copies to all the streets.
Lǐzhèng picks up a stack of papers from the desk and hands them out dutifully.
Thank you, Sir.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: This is my duty. As for Gětiān, we shall put him on hold untill after the Dùshuò Festival according to the law.
One more thing. Have we found the horse and the proof?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Not yet. The horse taking that foreign lady away might still be under the control of Gětiān. There was no trace of them when our people chased them out of the city.
I understand, given the road conditions in the morning rain. Looks like we will have to continue with the search after it stops.
But I don't think a horse carrying a blind woman can go far enough to escape. I'll lead the search squad myself next time.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Thank you, Fǎcáo.

The imposing figure, with his back to the entryway, habitually presses down on the short sword at his waist, adjusting the position of the blade. Then waves his hand again to show that he doesn't need to concern himself with such matters.

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: I'm only doing my job. Where is the Zhílǐ?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Are you referring to Jiǔ Niángzǐ, or the former one?

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: The one who went back to her hometown.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: We haven't heard anything from her yet. Perhaps it will come after the Dùshuò Festival.

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: Noted. Jiǔ Niángzǐ is still green, so please help me take care of the Zhící before the former one comes back.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: I will. She is kind-hearted. That's why I recommended her for this position. It will be my responsibility if she makes any mistakes.

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: Well, there are so many things to do before the New Year. It's fine, even if she makes a mistake or two. Don't push her too hard.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: That's what I thought. If you find any evidence or the two foreigners, please let me know.
Fǎcáo rises nimbly while folding the documents, as he prepares to bid his farewell, he is stopped by Lǐzhèng's raised hand.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Oh, another thing, the New Year's Feast tonight. You're welcome to Jiǔ Niángzǐ's tavern with your relatives.

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: The tavern? Are the people around the merchants hub going too?

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Yes. She is hosting a feast for the neighbors.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: It is the New Year's Eve Vigil, followed by the first day of Dùshuò Festival.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: It is an annual tradition at the tavern.

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: Shuòrì, the New Year ...

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Right, another year of the Zhíxú ...

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Hopefully, the Yuān Temple, which worships the Zhíxú, will bring us good news.
Having said his piece, leaving only a moment of silence. The two of them look out the window, toward the eaves of the broken bridge and the temple flickering in the misty rain.
